title: Holy, holy, holy (Apocalypse 4)
hookLine: around the throne the living creatures never stop singing

cards: A door again, but this time it opens the other way. John writes: "behold a door was opened in heaven." A voice like a trumpet says, come up here.
Suddenly John isn't looking at seven small churches in Asia anymore. Until now the book has kept its eyes on earth; here the camera swings up, through a doorway into the center of everything.
And what John sees first isn't a battle, or a beast, or a timeline. It's worship.

teach.h: JASPER, EMERALD, A SEA OF GLASS.
teach.b: John reaches for words. The one on the throne looks like jasper and sardine stone. A rainbow like emerald circles the throne.
Lightning, thunder, seven burning lamps, and before it a sea of glass like crystal. Around it sit twenty-four elders in white, with gold crowns.
Close around the throne, four living creatures: one like a lion, one like a calf, one with a man's face, one like a flying eagle, each with six wings and covered with eyes.
Then the sound, in the Douay-Rheims: "And they rested not day and night, saying: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come." Rested not: the song never stops.

John's readers would have heard an echo. Long before, in the temple, the prophet Isaiah saw the seraphim crying to each other: "Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God of hosts, all the earth is full of his glory."
Holy is often explained as set apart, other, nothing like us; saying it three times piles it as high as the words will go. Then the elders fall down and cast their crowns before the throne.
Every honor they have, they give back. Catholics know this song.
At every Mass, at the end of the Preface, the priest speaks of joining the angels and saints in their hymn, and the people sing the Sanctus: holy, holy, holy.

teach.h: HOLY, HOLY, HOLY, LORD GOD ALMIGHTY.
teach.b: The Church says the Mass on earth joins the worship John saw through that open door.
Later Christian tradition made the four creatures symbols of the four Gospel writers: Matthew the man, Mark the lion, Luke the calf, John the eagle.

how: At every Mass, at the end of the Preface, the priest invites the people to join the angels and saints, and all sing or say the Sanctus, Holy, Holy, Holy, drawn from Isaiah 6 and Apocalypse 4.

o: keep your crown as a reward you earned.
fall down and cast your crown before the throne.

practice: Picture what John saw: the open door, the rainbow, the sea of glass, the creatures with their wings, the elders laying down their crowns, and let it be bright and loud.

Then imagine the song has been going on the whole time, through every ordinary minute of your day. If you pray, join it softly, holy, holy, holy, once on each out-breath; if not, just listen in your mind to a song that never rests.

wordCard.voice: Holy. Set apart, wholly other. Sung three times by the creatures around the throne, and by the people at every Mass. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: holy, holy, holy (Apocalypse 4:8), echoing Isaiah's Hebrew qadosh.
